title: feat(state): the chain — a receipt rests on the decision and change proof, a closure names the receipt
context:
Gate 4's cross-domain chain (incident → engineering decision → change proof →
closure) becomes a contract feature, run end to end through the one binding by
three principals over one store (repository partition + organization drawer).

- ActionReceipt.rests_on (additive, optional): DependencyRefs — the decision the
  action implements, the change proof for the shipped revision (external ref,
  system hunch / change_proof keyed by proof_id + content_hash), the commitment or
  incident it answers. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: A receipt carries `rests_on` (DependencyRefs, additive): the decision it implements, the change proof (external ref, system hunch / change_proof keyed by proof_id + content_hash), the commitment or incident it answers; a record ref may carry a partition `scope`. A commitment carries `closed_by` (additive): the receipt that fulfilled it. The binding verifies grants first, then what it holds (absent / hash-moved / wrong-partition refs are typed conflicts naming the way out; a ref into a partition the store does not hold is a pointer); a closure must name a succeeded/verified receipt on a done commitment and its change event's cause is that receipt. Reads put fulfilled commitments in `done` beside their receipts and concatenate every done receipt's rests_on into depends_on. Write results and change events hash the record ON FILE (the store enriches on put); the ledger journal keeps the payload hash for replay.
consequences: Adds dependency: node:test, node:assert/strict, node:child_process, node:fs, node:os, node:path.
alternatives_rejected: Auto-close a commitment when a receipt with the same subject lands — rejected: subject overlap is not fulfilment; two commitments on one customer would both close, and nobody named the receipt.
A new `incident` facet with its own lifecycle — rejected: an incident is an entity with a CRM pointer; the chain needs links between existing facets, not a fourth kind of thing to keep current.

Have the state layer fetch and verify the change proof from the repository on write — rejected: never-in-request-path; the proof is a credential-free pointer (id + content hash) the reader resolves with `records`, grants first.

Refuse every rests_on ref the store cannot verify — rejected: an organization drawer legitimately points at a repository the server does not host; unverifiable-here is a pointer, only absent/moved/misplaced in a held partition is a conflict.

Keep reporting the pre-store payload hash in write results — rejected: a private-mode decision gains valid_from on put, so a receipt resting on that hash would be refused as moved; results and events hash what is on file, replay matches the payload.
rejected_tripwires: a commitment reaches status done through subject matching or a timer, without a receipt id
a rests_on record ref is accepted with a hash the held partition does not have
WriteResult.record_hash differs from stateHash of the record `records` returns for the same id

evidence: synth:provider=deterministic, substance written by the agent that made the change
